statement: Whether the Mwari cult was Great Zimbabwe's state religion during the site's 13th-15th century floruit is genuinely contested, not settled. Some earlier/popular accounts and the "Mbire" oral migration tradition treat the cult as continuous with or originating at Great Zimbabwe. David Beach argued documentary/oral linkage between the archaeological site and the cult during that period is weak — the cult's source-rich documented history begins with its 17th-18th century Rozvi (Changamire dynasty) association and Matopos/Njelele shrine geography. Richard Werbner (Kalanga fieldwork) argues further that the cult historically was never structurally bound to any specific state/polity at all. Innocent Pikirayi (The Zimbabwe Culture, AltaMira Press, 2001) cautions against reading the cult as a mere instrument of state power even in its later, better-documented Rozvi-era form.
scholarly_disagreement: Whether the Mwari cult's political-religious association with Great Zimbabwe specifically (as opposed to its later, better-documented Rozvi/Matopos-era form) is real continuity or backward extrapolation from later evidence.

sources.citation: Pikirayi, Innocent. The Zimbabwe Culture: Origins and Decline of Southern Zambezian States. AltaMira Press, 2001.

interpretations.position: The Mwari cult originated at or was continuous with Great Zimbabwe, later moving to the Matopos with Rozvi political power

holders.name: Proponents of the "Mbire migration" oral tradition, per the surveyed literature

interpretations.strongest_case: Oral tradition places cult officials migrating south from the Lake regions with Karanga clans in the 14th century.

interpretations.position: The cult's documented history begins later (17th-18th c. Rozvi era); its presence at Great Zimbabwe specifically is inferential, not independently evidenced
interpretations.strongest_case: No archaeological dating specific to the Njelele shrine or documentary linkage to Great Zimbabwe's own floruit has been established; Werbner's Kalanga fieldwork finds no structural state-cult binding at any period.
